S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

symptom.disease_info: Body Dysmorphic Disorder is characterized by a persistent preoccupation with one or more perceived defects in appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others, accompanied by repetitive behaviors or mental acts in response to those concerns. It is distinguished from ordinary appearance dissatisfaction by the degree of distress, time consumed, and functional impairment, and from eating-disorder body concerns when the focus is not primarily weight or body fat. The course is often chronic or waxing and waning, with clinical presentation sometimes becoming evident after social transitions, relationship stress, injury, illness, or increased scrutiny of appearance.

patient.stressor: After Han Yuen’s divorce, he moved into a smaller apartment and found himself unexpectedly re-entering social life through family gatherings, board-game nights, and occasional dating apps where recent photos felt unavoidable. What began as discomfort with how weathered his face looked in jobsite photos and phone-camera selfies gradually became a fixed concern about a perceived facial flaw that coworkers and relatives either did not notice or considered minor. Over time, his checking and appearance-related routines started delaying him before work, making him avoid being photographed at construction sites, and causing him to skip some social events he had previously enjoyed. He first sought help through repeated cosmetic and dermatology consultations, and after one clinician noted the mismatch between his distress and the visible finding, Han accepted a referral for psychiatric evaluation.

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: I’m here because I can’t stop seeing this rough, sunken-looking patch on my face in photos and in the mirror, like one side of me looks old and beat-up, even though people keep saying they barely notice anything.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: Before work or going to my sister’s game night, I’ll keep checking the bathroom mirror, turning my face under different lights, rubbing at the spot, and sometimes I wear a hat low or just make an excuse not to go if I think it looks too obvious.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve been late getting out the door for construction jobs, and I’ve started dodging site photos and skipping some family game nights because I don’t want people looking at my face.
